## Snapshot
Alphabet is the full-stack AI franchise: Google Services (Search, YouTube, subscriptions/devices — ~$90B/qtr, the cash engine), Google Cloud (GCP + Workspace + Wiz security, now the marginal growth driver), and Other Bets (Waymo, etc.). The differentiated edge vs. other hyperscalers is owning the *entire* vertical stack — frontier models (Gemini), custom silicon (TPU, Axion CPU), networking/OCS, data centers, and apps/agents — which management frames as the source of leading power/perf efficiency and ROIC (Q1 FY26, 2026-04-29). Sits at the center of the AI capex cycle as both a demand anchor (its own ~$180-190B C26 capex) and an emerging merchant-silicon supplier (external TPU sales begin late C26). The TPU franchise is the swing variable: Asia supply-chain checks now size total TPU production at ~3.1-3.2mn units in 2026, potentially doubling to 5-6mn in 2027 (~5mn via Broadcom + ~1mn via MediaTek) — alongside AWS Trainium one of the two dominant merchant-ASIC programs (Jefferies Techknowledge, 2025-12-17). On the model side, Gemini 2.5 Pro is tied #1 on LM Arena and recognized as a leading cost-effective frontier model that has displaced OpenAI on coding/overall leaderboards (JPM OpenAI initiation; JPM Anthropic deep-dive, 2025-09-18).

**🆕🔴🔴 2026-09-07 — THE FIRST THIRD-PARTY INFERENCE BENCHMARK OF IRONWOOD AGAINST BLACKWELL IS OUT, AND TPU WINS ON THE METRIC BUYERS ACTUALLY USE.** (SemiAnalysis · Alec Ibarra, Cam Quilici, Bryan Shan, Wenyao Gao, Daniel Nishball, Zane Fong and **Dylan Patel** — "TPU Inference Externalization Full Steam Ahead", **2026-09-07**; *independent paid research, NOT a bank — no rating, no price target, no house model*)
- 🔴 **"Today, we are publishing the FIRST THIRD-PARTY INFERENCE RESULTS for TPUv7 Ironwood on InferenceX Official Preview. In our apples-to-apples comparisons against B200/B300, Ironwood delivers UP TO 50% BETTER PERFORMANCE PER DOLLAR."**
- **The unit economics, stated three ways so they are not conflated:**
  - **At 100 tokens/s/user interactivity: Ironwood ≈ $0.181 per million total tokens vs $0.222 (B200) and $0.276 (B300)** — ~19% cheaper than B200 and ~34% cheaper than B300, *at the same per-user generation speed*, on an EXTERNAL TPU TCO (i.e. what a customer pays).
  - **At 20 tok/s/user Ironwood also leads on RAW throughput: 9,364 total tokens/s/chip vs 8,903 (B200) and 8,925 (B300)** — ~5% higher — which combined with the lower hourly cost gives **+50.4% tokens per dollar vs B200 and +96.0% vs B300.**
  - **On GOOGLE'S INTERNAL TCO of $1.03/chip-hour, the perf-per-dollar advantage at concurrency 256 rises to +76.7% vs B200 and +130.2% vs B300** — but with a latency penalty: **TPU mean TTFT 5.41s vs 3.75s (B200) and 2.40s (B300)** at that concurrency.
  - At a 20-second median response time the Pareto curves put **TPU at ~$0.098/M tokens vs $0.106 (B200) and $0.132 (B300)** — ~8% and ~25% cheaper.
- ⚠️⚠️ **THREE DISCIPLINES ENFORCED BEFORE ANY OF THIS IS USED. (1) THE HEADLINE IS AGGREGATED-VS-AGGREGATED. On a DISAGG-vs-DISAGG basis "GB200/300 NVL72 is MORE COMPETITIVE on perf per dollar" today, because the external TPU stack has no optimised disaggregated path yet; SemiAnalysis expects the gap to close "within a few months" but has NOT yet published that comparison, and on the agg-vs-disagg cut GB300 NVL72 holds a ~30% perf/$ advantage in the middle of the latency curve. (2) NVIDIA STILL WINS ON FP4 — "TPUv7 does not have native FP4 computation thus on FP4, NVIDIA GPUs still maintain the lead"; SemiAnalysis expects that to flip with **TPUv8i**, which has native FP4 and which they believe "will be competitive to Rubin NVL72." (3) THE INTERNAL-TCO NUMBER IS NOT A CUSTOMER PRICE, and the 50-96% range "applies to this datapoint specifically, rather than every latency target" — SemiAnalysis says so in its own text; carry the caveat with the number.**
- 🔴 **The externalisation MECHANISM is the actual news, not the benchmark: the new TorchTPU backend makes TPUs a NATIVE PyTorch device (via PyTorch's PrivateUse1 extension point) instead of translating PyTorch → JAX through TorchAX. It "remains in private beta and will be OPEN-SOURCED around mid-OCTOBER during the PyTorch Conference."** vLLM and SGLang maintainers could then add TPUs to the day-0 support list they currently reserve for NVIDIA (with "passable day-0 coverage for AMD"). Bring-up model is **Qwen3.5-397B in FP8**, with **Kimi K3 and GLM5.3** to follow. Inferact, RadixArk and Red Hat are named as collaborators.
- 🔴 **Anthropic sizing restated: "[[ANTHROPIC]] loves TPUs and committed to OVER ONE MILLION of them (around 400k+ in DIRECT PURCHASES and 600k+ RENTED through GCP)"**, and SemiAnalysis projects **Anthropic becomes the biggest user of TPUs, surpassing DeepMind's own use by 2029.**
- ➤ **Why this matters more than a benchmark: the CUDA moat has always been argued as a software-DISTRIBUTION problem, not a silicon problem. A native PyTorch device plus day-0 vLLM/SGLang coverage is the first credible attack on the distribution half — and SemiAnalysis's stated reason for believing it lands is organisational, not technical: "unlike AMD, which is still learning how to build a test-first software culture, Google has decades of software engineering experience and an extremely well established quality-driven culture."** ⚠️ **NOTHING ADOPTED into estimates. This is an independent author's first-look preview of ONE model at ONE precision on a stack that is not yet open source.**

- ⚠️ **ON CANNIBALISING [[NVDA]] THE EXPERT REFUSES THE CLEAN ANSWER: *"**Yes and no.** Definitely, if a customer doesn't invest in Google TPUs, that demand might go to Nvidia as well. **Or the budget or the project might be on hold itself because it is not being fulfilled** because of the supply issue."*** Then the lock-in leg, which is the structural bull argument: *"once someone starts in a particular ecosystem… the **switching costs** from one ecosystem to another is kind of **prohibitive**, because they have to build all the knowledge base, all the rules, again"*, and a TPU buyer *"will start to spend a part of their cloud into the GCP as well."* ➤ **His framing of the pull-through, which is the sharpest sentence in the call: *"the **chip is more like the wedge, and the data platform is more like the contract**"* — a TPU deployment drags **BigQuery, Vertex, storage and networking** behind it.**
- 🔴 **PRICING — THE FIRST EXTERNAL PRICE POINTS ON THIS PAGE, AND THE QUOTE-ONLY MODEL IS DELIBERATE: for an external buyer *"there's **no disclosed public price. It's primarily quote only**"* (older generations do carry list prices), negotiated on **number of systems, TPU generation, support and warranty terms** — and the reason is control: *"**Google is choosing who to give the chips** rather than the other way around."* The marks he gives, ⚠️ **which are RENTAL rates, not system prices: ~$12 per chip-hour on demand · ~$6 on DWS Flex-start · ~$5.50 on a three-year commitment.** ⚠️⚠️ **DO NOT NET THESE AGAINST THIS PAGE'S $/GW OR $23-34k-PER-CHIP MARKS — a chip-hour rental rate, a per-chip system price and a $/GW figure are three different bases (`_meta/assumptions.md`).** ➤ **And the customer's yardstick is moving: *"more and more clients are looking towards measuring it around **cost per useful output** rather than just looking at the speed"* — infra cost ÷ completed training runs, ÷ useful tokens at the required SLA, ÷ completed agent tasks, because *"a cheaper accelerator that requires maybe twice as many chips is not cheaper"* and *"a faster chip sitting idle… doesn't mean it's more economical."***
- **REVENUE MODEL — FOUR LAYERS, and it is the best answer this page has to "is an external TPU sale a one-off?":** ① predominantly an **upfront hardware system sale recognised on delivery**; ② **attached software, support and services** — on-prem platform licensing plus the runtime/compiler/orchestration layer (**XLA, Pathways, MaxText**), cluster management, spares and field-engineering contracts; ③ **hybrid/burst consumption back to GCP** (on-prem TPU owners still burst for training runs and overflow inference) plus **data-platform pull-through**; ④ the **generational replacement cycle** — buyers move the newest silicon onto their most critical workloads and cascade the old. *"Right now the model is **more hardware heavy than a conventional cloud consumption** model, but over time the software revenue and support revenue will also start to get recognized."* ⚠️ **Asked point-blank how the economics of selling TPUs outright compare with renting the same capacity through GCP, he declined — *"Not really. I will not be able to comment on that"* — so the merchant-vs-rental margin question this page has been unable to close from ANY source stays OPEN.**
- **GO-TO-MARKET — THE CYCLE IS LONG AND POWER-GATED: 7 to 18 months end-to-end** for a large external purchase (**2-4 months technical evaluation and porting · 4-6 weeks commercial negotiation · 4-12 months physical deployment**), gated in his stated order by ① **power availability and facility readiness**, ② **software-porting effort and framework mismatch**, ③ **Google's own chip allocation to the customer**, ④ **JAX/Pallas skills scarcity** (*"engineers are scarce… need a lot of hiring or retraining"*, at *"premium salaries"*), ⑤ **ISV and tooling certification**. **Deal sizes: *"at least six figures in most cases"* for the first two-to-three months of integration, with the contract intent *"at least to go to seven figures within a year"*, and in many cases *"multiple seven figures."*** ➤ **A 7-18-month cycle starting now lands the bulk of external revenue in 2027 — consistent with management's "vast majority in 2027" framing rather than ahead of it.**
- **CONVERSION BY SEGMENT, HIS OWN RANKING: frontier AI labs HIGHEST** (*"they write JAX natively… they evaluate ECONOMICS rather than the feasibility"*) **→ hyperscaler peers high but STAGED** (Meta rents first, buys later, 12-24 months, in tranches) **→ HPC / research / capital markets moderate-to-high** (compiler-level engineers, stable workloads) **→ large PyTorch-native enterprises LOW → neoclouds LOWEST so far.** **Why POCs fail to convert, in his order: ① *"the porting cost might exceed the savings… that's probably the biggest one"*, ② PyTorch training-stack coupling, ③ capacity cannot be committed on the buyer's timeline, ④ the results are simply better on NVIDIA and *"they don't want to compromise on the results."*** **TAM framing, and it is a NET-NEW segmentation for this page: ~**10-15%** of his customer base are optimal candidates to BUY AND OPERATE TPU systems directly today; another ~**25-40%** are good candidates to CONSUME TPU capacity through GCP, a TPU neocloud or a **GSI-managed AI platform**, of which ~**15-30%** are good TPU customers who will never own the hardware.** ➤ **The GSI channel is the leg nobody on this page has modelled: the end customer gets TPU economics *"without taking… the residual value risk or hardware maintenance or massive CAPEX"*, and the GSI carries it.**
- ⚠️ **THE NEOCLOUD LEG IS THE SWING FACTOR AND IT IS PRICED IN NEITHER DIRECTION: *"right now we don't see too much of demand from NeoClouds, but yes, NeoClouds can absolutely become their major TPU customers… structurally… one of their most important external customer groups."* Why they would, in his order: **better return per megawatt and per dollar of deployed capital** than the NVIDIA alternative; **not wanting all revenue dependent on one vendor's CUDA ecosystem and one allocation process**; **inability to obtain enough latest-generation NVIDIA capacity** (*"they can simply add TPUs rather than leaving all these customer demand unserved"*); **workload routing — v8T for large-scale training, v8i for inference, reasoning, MoE and RL**; and financeability — *"TPU deployment becomes much easier to finance if a customer like [[ANTHROPIC]] signs a long-term take."*** ✅ **The v8T/v8i workload split independently corroborates the Hot Chips read already logged here on 08-31/09-01 (UBS · Arcuri; @QQ_Timmy) that Google is deliberately SEPARATING training and inference silicon.** ⚠️ *the generation labels arrive ASR-garbled in the extract ("8T"/"8I") and are decoded against the Hot Chips and [[AVGO]]-call naming already on this page — not guessed.*
- ⚠️ **THE BEAR LIST, FROM A SELLER — the four reasons a customer scores TPU as ROI-NEGATIVE: ① **utilisation** (a well-priced chip at low utilisation is a bad ROI), ② **there is NO SECONDARY MARKET for TPUs versus a strong one for NVIDIA → higher depreciation / residual-value risk**, ③ the **software-ecosystem gap** (*"improving rapidly, but it could very well take longer time"*), ④ **repurposability** — *"TPUs are primarily AI focused, while… Nvidia… are more broader"*, so they are harder to redeploy when the next generation lands.** **AND THE PLATFORM SCORECARD: on RAW SILICON *"TPU has kind of closed the gap"*; Google's advantage is *"vertical integration across chip, fabric, compiler, model and cloud"* / *"vertical co-design at massive scale"*; its disadvantages are *"the software ecosystem"* and supply, plus *"no secondary… market, no merchant channels"* and a talent pool where *"JAX or Pallas engineers are probably a fraction of the CUDA population."* ⚠️ **AND THE DISCIPLINE LINE THIS WIKI SHOULD ADOPT: *"right now there's **no credible single public benchmark** which… looks across TPUs, Rubins, Trainium 3, MI450, because all these vendors use different precisions, different workloads, system assumptions."*** ➤ **[[NVDA]]'s named edge is CUDA/ecosystem breadth; [[AMZN]]'s Trainium edge is *"economics inside the AWS ecosystem… possibly 30 to 40% better price performance than comparable other GPU instances"*; [[AMD]]'s is memory capacity, open architecture and rack-scale alternatives.**
- **OPEN-WEIGHT MODELS — he lands on the same side as this page's 08-12 MS work and nets it POSITIVE for TPU units: cheaper open models have *"two opposing effects"* (more enterprises clear the self-hosting threshold vs less compute needed per workload), and *"the first one probably will win… lower model cost will be able to bring more enterprises across the self-hosting threshold"*, turning model spending into **infrastructure spending** and creating *"a **new enterprise AI factory buyer**."***
[Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_09_02_tpu_call_susq_2_set_26.html)

"Never been stronger" is a statement about Google's absolute volume, not its rank or its share of Broadcom's book. Both facts are from the same call.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-26 — GOOGLE PUT NUMBERS ON THE TPU v8 SRAM TIER AT HOT CHIPS, AND THE SRAM-vs-HBM GAP IT DISCLOSED IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR THE 8i VARIANT.** (William Blair · **Sebastien Naji** w/ Anna Bilbao, *"AI Infrastructure Competition Heats Up; Takeaways From Hot Chips 2026"*, 2026-08-26, 9pp — **GOOG OUTPERFORM, px $343.34.** ⚠️ Router returned broker `?` and no date on this file; both corrected from the note.)
- 🔴 **THE NUMBER: *"Google quantified the advantage of **TPU 8i's enlarged on-chip SRAM, citing roughly 150-200 TB/s of bandwidth and 1 TO 2 ns access latency versus 10-15 TB/s and 150-200 ns for HBM**."*** ➜ **That is ~10-15x the bandwidth at ~100x lower latency — and it is the quantitative case for a dedicated inference part with a large SRAM tier, i.e. exactly the architectural bet [[CEREBRAS]] and Groq make. Read it against the HBM-density debate on [themes/hbm-memory](themes/hbm-memory.md): if the latency-sensitive layer moves on-die, HBM's role narrows toward capacity rather than bandwidth on that class of workload.** ⚠️ **No capacity figure for the SRAM is given, which is the binding constraint on the whole idea — SRAM bandwidth is worthless if the working set does not fit, and dynamic KV cache is the thing that does not fit.**
- 🔴 **CONNECTIVITY DETAIL, NET-NEW: *"2.4 TB/s of BIDIRECTIONAL I/O bandwidth per **TPU 8t** chip, **SIX ICI LINKS using 224G SerDes**, and the use of **WATER-COOLED OPTICS in the 8t tray**."*** ➜ **Water-cooled optics in a shipping TPU tray is a concrete optical-thermal datapoint for [themes/optical-cpo](themes/optical-cpo.md) and for the optics complex ([[COHR]], [[LITE]]) — it says the optical layer is now inside the liquid-cooling envelope on Google's platform.**
- 🔴 **AND THE SCALE-UP DOMAIN, WHICH IS THE HEADLINE COMPARISON: *"Google's **TPUv8t has a scale-up domain as high as 9,600 CHIPS**"* — against **72 GPUs** for both [[NVDA]]'s and [[AMD]]'s flagship racks and **2,048 chips** for [[OPENAI]]'s Jalapeño.** ⚠️⚠️ **These are NOT like-for-like: a 72-GPU NVLink domain and a 9,600-chip ICI domain differ in interconnect, coherence and per-chip capability, and William Blair presents them as scale-up domain sizes rather than as equivalent systems. Do not rank them as one series. What IS legitimate to take away is the note's own framing: *"the debate is shifting toward WHICH ARCHITECTURE CAN TRANSLATE THAT THEORETICAL CAPABILITY INTO THE HIGHEST SUSTAINED UTILIZATION AND LOWEST COST PER TOKEN"* — i.e. domain size has stopped being the differentiator.**
- ✅ **A SMALL BUT REAL PRODUCTIVITY DATAPOINT ON GOOGLE'S OWN DESIGN LOOP: *"the company highlighted the role of AI-ASSISTED CHIP DESIGN, noting that optimization **REDUCED AREA AND INCREASED FLOPs BY 5%-6%**."*** ⚠️ Vendor claim, single generation, no baseline stated.

A competitor's characterisation of Google's own position, not a Google statement.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/AI_Infrastructure_Competition_Heats_Up_Takeaways_From_Hot_Chips_2026.html)

- **The new build:** **$84bn of TPU-related Cloud revenue in 2027 and $108bn in 2028**, on **0.3 GW sold in 2H26, 3.2 GW in 2027 and 4.2 GW in 2028** — the 2027/28 TPU revenue estimates are **+35% vs prior**. Total **Google Cloud revenue estimates rise ~6%/~7%**.
- 🔴 **The mix consequence, which is the actual thesis change: MS now assumes GOOGL Cloud reaches ~50% of TOTAL company EBIT by 2028** (TMTB's relay of the same note says **~48%**), *"although lower-margin TPU sales keep Cloud margins around ~37-40%."*
- **EPS moves only low-single-digits on the revision.** *"The bigger stock catalyst is **Gemini 4** — if GOOGL can return to the frontier then the valuation should re-rate higher to a **low-20s EPS multiple**."* **Brian sees $18-20 EPS in 2028 (MS $18.50).**
⚠️⚠️ **BASIS WARNING: the ~$27bn/GW is TPU *PRICING* — i.e. REVENUE per GW sold — and must NOT be netted against, or chained with, the $/GW BUILD-COST anchors carried in `_meta/assumptions.md` and on the datacenter pages. Different denominators.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-25 — GOOGLE IS ALSO THE CLEAREST EQUITY-FUNDING DATAPOINT IN THE HYPERSCALER COMPLEX.** *"GOOGL is an important equity-funding datapoint: it has **cut annual buybacks from >$60B to ZERO and issued $50B of equity in 2Q26, creating >$110B of incremental cash capacity for AI investment**. MS expects SBC-related dilution across hyperscalers to increase as companies conserve cash"* (MS · Todd Castagno, via MS TMT, 2026-08-25). **Sector frame from the same note: MS expects hyperscalers to spend >$1.2tn of cash capex in 2027 against ~$1tn of aggregate operating cash flow, forcing leases/SPVs, public debt, lower buybacks, equity issuance, customer prepayments and vendor-supported financing.**

Logged because direct HBM procurement is a structural cost advantage for the TPU stack vs buying an NVDA rack with memory embedded in it — and because it is a falsifiable claim about Google's purchasing.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-22/24 — THE TPU STORY GOT FOUR SEPARATE UPGRADES THIS WEEK, AND THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE IS ARCHITECTURAL RATHER THAN COMMERCIAL: A MOVE FROM A 3D TO A 6D TORUS WOULD QUADRUPLE OPTICAL CONTENT PER TPU.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-24 — MS RAISES THE TPU 1P SALE PRICE 35% (TO $27bn/GW) AND THE GROSS MARGIN 10pts (TO 30%), PUTTING **$84bn / $108bn** OF TPU REVENUE INSIDE GOOGLE CLOUD IN '27/'28 AND TAKING CLOUD TO ~50% OF COMPANY EBIT BY '28 — YET THE PT DOES NOT MOVE.** (MS · **Brian Nowak** + Gregory Gao / Nikhil Javeri / Julian Herrera / Kavya Narayanan, **Overweight, PT $400 maintained**, "$200bn of 1P TPU Revenue on the Way and 3 Catalysts Ahead", 2026-08-24, 20pp)
- **What changed and why.** MS previously modelled GOOGL selling TPU racks/systems in 1P relationships at **$20bn/GW on a 20% gross margin**. It now uses **$27bn/GW at a 30% gross margin.** Two triggers, both external: (1) *"recent press reports point to GOOGL committing to supply **~1mn TPUs (which we estimate is ~1.3 GW) for ~$35bn**, which would translate to **~$27bn/GW**"*; (2) *"GOOGL's expanded custom-silicon agreement with **[[MRVL]]** … is consistent with (and arguably supportive of) **TPU pricing/ASPs running HIGHER than we had assumed**."*
- 🔴 **A CROSS-SOURCE RECONCILIATION THAT NOBODY HAS WRITTEN DOWN, FLAGGED AS AN INFERENCE NOT A VERIFIED IDENTITY.** The **same ~$35bn** appears the same day in **The Information (Dakin Campbell, 2026-08-24)** as *the June financing* in which *"Apollo teamed up with Blackstone to raise debt, **buy the TPUs and lease them to [[ANTHROPIC]]**… **[[AVGO]] agreed to backstop $29 billion of the overall debt through a residual value guarantee**"* — **~82% coverage**, with the riskiest tranche unbackstopped. **If MS's ~$35bn TPU supply commitment and The Information's ~$35bn TPU financing are the same transaction, then the entire ~1.3GW purchase is ~100% debt-funded at the asset level, with Broadcom (not Google, not Anthropic) carrying 82% of the residual risk — and MS's $27bn/GW price is a price struck against a guaranteed balance sheet, not an arm's-length cash buyer.** ⚠️ **Neither source names the counterparty of the other; treat as a strong same-transaction inference to be confirmed, not as fact.**
- **The volume ladder (new to this page):** **0.3 GW of TPU systems sold in 2H:26, 3.2 GW in '27, 4.2 GW in '28** → **$84bn ('27) / $108bn ('28) of TPU-related Google Cloud revenue, +35% / +37% vs MS's prior estimates.**
- **What it does to Cloud.** TPU-related Cloud **revenue growth 118% in '27 (vs 106% prior)** and **EBIT growth 137% (vs 105%)**; total Google Cloud forecasts **+6% / +7% in '27/'28**; Cloud EBIT **+2% / +2%**; **Cloud reaches ~48-50% of company-wide EBIT as soon as '28.**
- ⚠️ **The margin is the concession, and it is the number to watch:** reported Cloud margins come **DOWN slightly, 38%/41% → 37%/40% in '27/'28**, because TPU sales are *"lower margin but larger incremental revenue."* Excluding TPUs (**~30% EBIT margin**) and the **[[SPCX]] compute deal** (an explicit named margin headwind), **core Cloud incremental margins stay ~50% through '27.** 🔴 **So the 1P TPU business is dilutive to the reported Cloud margin by construction — a Cloud-margin miss in '27 may be MIX, not deterioration, and this page should not read it as demand weakness without checking the TPU revenue line first.**
- **Company-level:** revenue **+2% / +3%** in '27/'28; **'Other CoR' taken UP 4% / 6%** to align ex-TPU incremental margins; **EPS +1% / +2%.**
- 🔴 **A NEW DISCLOSURE TO TRACK, NAMED BY THE ANALYST: _"we will continue to pay attention to GOOGL's new disclosure of INVENTORY ON THE BALANCE SHEET for signs of buildup/drawdown as these sales begin to kick in."_** ➜ **Google now carries an inventory line because it is selling hardware. That line is the cleanest early read on whether the 1P TPU sell-through is tracking the 0.3/3.2/4.2 GW ladder.**
- **Valuation unchanged and explicitly multiple-limited:** PT **$400** = **~24x the average of the new '27/'28 EPS of $15 / $18.50**, ~15% upside, *"implying a ~20% premium to peers on a growth-adjusted basis (whereas GOOGL currently trades at a 5% premium to peers)."*
- **The three catalysts, in MS's own priority order.** (1) 🔴 **Gemini 4 (late '26 / early '27) — *"the most important catalyst to re-rate GOOGL back to levels last seen post Gemini 3 release (Nov. '25)"*.** (2) **Gemini Flash and the efficient/low-cost model suite**, *"as enterprises become increasingly budget conscious in their AI implementations"* — i.e. MS is explicitly underwriting the cheap-token side of the [[themes/tokenmaxxing]] debate as a GOOGL positive. (3) **Fully-scaled product roll-outs across Google's corpuses** (the Google I/O set) to prove more durable Search/YouTube growth than appreciated.
- ⚠️ **Note the framing gap: MS's headline says "$200bn of 1P TPU revenue on the way," which is the '27 + '28 SUM ($84bn + $108bn = $192bn), not an annual run-rate. Do not quote $200bn as a yearly number.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-20 — THE CAPITAL-STRUCTURE SIDE, IN TWO PARTS: BARCLAYS STAMPS THE EQUITY RAISE AS A MILESTONE BECAUSE ALPHABET HAD NOT RAISED EQUITY SINCE THE IPO, AND MORGAN STANLEY'S CREDIT DESK SHOWS ALPHABET'S NEW BONDS *TIGHTENING* WHILE THE REST OF THE HQ HYPERSCALER COMPLEX WIDENED — INCLUDING THE BIGGEST YEN BOND ON RECORD FROM A FOREIGN ISSUER.** (**Barclays · Ross Sandler + Tom O'Malley**, "U.S. Internet & Semiconductors — Charts Worth A Look: Unpacking AI Infrastructure 'Backstop 101'", **2026-08-13**; and **Morgan Stanley Global Credit Strategy** — Fernanda Lima, Carolyn Campbell, Vishwanath Tirupattur, Vishwas Patkar, James Egan — "AI Debt Financing Tracker: The Summer Spreads Turned Wider", **2026-08-20**.) [Barclays source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Barclays_U_S_Internet_Semiconductors_Charts_Worth_A_Look_Unpacking_AI_Infrastructure_Backstop_101_.html) · [MS Credit source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/USCREDIT_20260820_2103.html)
- 🔴 **THE GOOGLE-SPECIFIC DATAPOINT FROM BARCLAYS, AND IT IS A ONE-LINE FRAMING THAT THIS PAGE HAS BEEN MISSING: Barclays stamps Google's equity raise as "a new milestone in the AI buildout" — noting that ALPHABET HAD NOT RAISED EQUITY SINCE THE IPO.** ➜ **The page carries the raise itself ($80B→$85B, Jun'26: $30B public + $40B ATM + $10B Berkshire PP; largest US corporate equity offering ever) and Ben Thompson's See's-Candies/BNSF interpretation of it. What was missing was the *baseline*: this is not Alphabet leaning harder on a familiar funding channel, it is Alphabet opening a channel it had not used in ~22 years of being public. That is the cleanest single-sentence statement of how far the capital intensity has moved from the historical model, and it belongs alongside the FCF-negative debate rather than inside it.**
- **Barclays' surrounding frame, for scale (industry-level, not Google-specific): hyperscaler capex has borne $1.5 TRILLION since 2023 through '26, with several trillion more in coming years; the hyperscaler "FUNDING GAP" — operating cash flow less capex — COULD EXCEED $200BN IN '27; and the industry has natural limits around debt levels and power agreements, with Barclays writing "we seem to be approaching those limits in '27."** That is what opens the door to the new backstop structures — **upwards of $1 TRILLION in new compute financing backstopped by [[NVDA]] and [[AVGO]]**. ➜ **Google-relevant because this page already documents Google acting as a BACKSTOP PROVIDER itself, not just a capex spender: the conditional support behind [[ANTHROPIC]]'s Fluidstack datacenter leases across 1,428 MW (Epoch AI, 08-12) and the $44bn of off-balance-sheet lease guarantees (The Information, 07-26). Barclays' "approaching those limits in '27" is therefore a statement about the year Google's own guarantee book gets tested, not just about its peers' borrowing.** ⚠️ **The $1tn NVDA/AVGO-backstopped compute-financing figure is industry-level and is NOT a Google number — [[NVDA]]/[[AVGO]] read-through is owned elsewhere in the wiki.**
- 🆕 **THE BOND MARKS, WHICH ARE NET-NEW TO THIS PAGE — AND THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT.** Per MS Credit's mark-to-market table, the **new GOOGL USD issues priced 8/6/2026 both TIGHTENED: the '31 (4.88% coupon) went 60 → 56bp (−5bp) and the '36 (5.45%) went 85 → 81bp (−5bp)**, *while the broader high-quality hyperscaler complex was ~30bp WIDER year-to-date.* ➜ **A borrower whose new paper tightens into a widening sector is being treated as a credit outlier in the right direction — which is the market's answer to the capital-intensity bear case, priced rather than argued. Worth holding against the equity-side framing on this page (source-of-funds positioning, the FCF-negative debate): the debt market and the equity market are currently disagreeing about Alphabet's capital plan.**
- 🆕 **AND THE FUNDING-CHANNEL DETAIL WORTH KEEPING: ALPHABET'S JPY DEAL WAS THE BIGGEST YEN BOND ON RECORD SOLD BY A FOREIGN ISSUER, AND ONLY TWO ISSUERS — ALPHABET AND [[AMZN]] — HAVE USED THE NON-DOLLAR MARKETS SO FAR THIS YEAR**, which is why MS notes sector concentration is less pronounced outside USD for now. ➜ **Directly relevant to the "approaching those limits in '27" question above: Alphabet is one of only two names demonstrating it can raise size OUTSIDE the dollar market, which is capacity its peers have not yet shown. Read with the equity-since-IPO point at the top of this block, the picture is a company that has spent 2026 opening every funding channel available to it — equity for the first time since the IPO, record-size yen, and USD paper that still tightens.**

The ratio FRAMEWORK remains Lumentum's (OFC Figure 2); the Virgo application is FUNDA's.**
- ⚠️ **AND A UNIT DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS, BECAUSE THE TWO 08-18/08-19 SOURCES MEASURE DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE NUMBERS LOOK CONTRADICTORY BUT ARE NOT: SemiAnalysis (08-18) says the 6D move "doubles each chip's ICI links from 6 to 12" — a **2x on LINKS**. FUNDA/GF (08-19) say wrap-around **OPTICAL PORTS** per chip go **1.5 → 6 — a 4x**. Both are right and FUNDA states both. Links are total ICI connections (copper + optical); optical ports are only the wrap-around links that must leave the rack. The optical share rises faster than the link count because edge length collapses from 4 to 2 and every chip becomes a boundary node. ➤ **Do NOT quote "2x" and "4x" as competing estimates of the same quantity — the investable number for the optical supply chain is the 4x on PORTS, not the 2x on links.**

- 🔴 **THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN OPINION — WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH CARRYING EVEN THOUGH THE PREMISE IS A RUMOUR. The building block stays a 64-chip rack; what changes is how those 64 chips are organised.** In 3D the rack is a **4×4×4** cube: each torus dimension is a closed ring of edge length k=4, only the wrap-around link that closes each ring must leave the rack optically, so optical ports per chip per dimension = 2/k = 0.5, i.e. **1.5 across three dimensions** — most chips are *interior* nodes wired in copper. In 6D the same 64 chips become **2⁶** (edge length k=2): in a ring of two, **both** chips are boundary chips, so 2/2 = **1 optical port per chip per dimension = 6 in total**, and **100% of chips need optical connectivity** (FUNDA). ➤ **So the 4x is the product of two 2x factors — dimensions ×2 (3→6) AND ports-per-dimension ×2 (0.5→1) as edge length falls from 4 to 2. It is NOT the intuitive 2x, and that distinction is the whole content of the call.** GF derives the identical result from the other end: external optical links per 64-chip block rise **96 → 384**, per-chip ports **1.5 → 6**.
- **The latency/topology case, which is why Google would want it:** for a 4,096-chip superpod a 3D torus (16×16×16 per FUNDA; 4×4×4 per GF's block framing) carries a worst-case diameter of **~24 hops vs ~12 hops for a 4⁶/2⁶ 6D arrangement** — halving the diameter compresses the **tail latency that MoE all-to-all traffic is most sensitive to**, and spreads traffic across 6 orthogonal paths, moving closer to non-blocking chip-to-chip communication (both houses). FUNDA's supporting mechanism: per the GShard paper, as experts scale 128 → 2,048, **all-to-all time rises from 16% to 36% of MoE + Transformer layer execution time** — i.e. the bottleneck the 6D move would be buying down is real and measured, independent of whether Google adopts it.
- **Precedents make it engineerable rather than exotic:** **IBM Blue Gene/Q (2011) was a 5D torus** (~97.8% of effective peak link utilisation on nearest-neighbour) and **Fujitsu's Fugaku (2020, Tofu-D) is a 6D mesh/torus interconnecting 158,976 nodes** with a hybrid of large and small dimensions — short-reach links on the small dimensions, optical on the large ones, *"conceptually similar to the proposed TPU architecture"* (FUNDA).
- **WHAT IS ALREADY DISCLOSED AND IS NOT A RUMOUR — the 8-series, which FUNDA reads as the thesis already playing out, and it splits cleanly into three layers Google itself names (scale-up in-pod / scale-out across pods / Jupiter front-end):**
  - **TPU 8t (training):** scale-up **retains the 3D torus** at higher ICI bandwidth; a single superpod scales to **9,600 chips** (vs 9,216 prior). The **Virgo** fabric serves scale-out — **a single fabric spanning 130K+ TPUs at ~47 Pb/s of bisection bandwidth, ~40% lower latency.**
  - **TPU 8i (inference):** **Boardfly** is an intra-pod (scale-up) restructuring, not a scale-out upgrade — interconnects **36 groups through OCS** with direct optical links, cutting network **diameter from ~16 to ~7 hops**.
  - ⚠️ 🔴 **AND HERE IS THE BASELINE TRAP FUNDA CALLS OUT EXPLICITLY, WHICH MATTERS FOR ANYONE MODELLING 8i OPTICAL CONTENT: "The right baseline for 8i is Google's long-standing small serving architecture rather than the 8,000-9,000-chip training superpod." The prior small pod was 256 chips (four 64-chip racks) connected ENTIRELY over copper — a scale-up optical/OCS ratio of ZERO. 8i takes all inter-rack connectivity optical, to roughly 1.25:1. "Anyone benchmarking 8i against the large superpod and concluding that optical intensity is down has simply picked the wrong baseline."** ➤ **Carry this as a standing unit guard on this page: 8i optical ratios are a copper-to-optics transition off a zero base, NOT a step-down from the 1.5:1 training figure. The two are different denominators and must not be netted.**
  - **Scale-out, per FUNDA's earlier framework now claimed as confirmed:** in-rack TH6 switches go **one → four-six per rack**, DCN bandwidth **up 4-6x**, the scale-out **OCS port ratio 0.2:1 → 1:1**, and the **optical-module ratio 1:1–1:2 → 1:3–1:4** with speeds **800G → 1.6T**. GF instead assumes scale-out at ~**1:2.5**, which with 6:1 scale-up gives an **aggregate TPU-to-port ratio of 1:8.5** — ⚠️ **GF's 1:8.5 aggregate and FUNDA's separate scale-up/scale-out ratios are DIFFERENT constructions of the same architecture; do not treat 1:8.5 as a consensus figure or add it to FUNDA's 6:1.**
- 💰 **THE COST FRAME, AND FUNDA LABELS IT AS AN UPPER BOUND IN ITS OWN WORDS — "a very optimistic, upper-bound estimate": ~$13,700 of optical + OCS content per TPU** on a *fully configured* 6D torus, covering **optical modules, OCS ports and cabling ONLY and excluding switching equipment**, at assumed ASPs of **~$700 for 1.6T DR8 (IMDD)** and **~$1,500 for 2.4T Coherent Lite**. Mapping caveat carried verbatim: the four scale-out modules sit at both ends of in-rack-switch→leaf→spine links while **OCS is deployed only at the spine, so ~4 modules map to ~1 OCS port, not one-to-one.** ➤ **Once switching is added back, FUNDA argues the order of magnitude resembles per-accelerator networking cost in [[NVDA]]'s NVL576 generation — but note Google already runs a 9,600-chip scale-up domain, "several times the size of NVIDIA's current scale-up," so the comparison is content-per-chip at very different domain sizes.**
- **The strategic read, which is the part that survives even if 6D never ships:** *"A single TPU is unlikely to outperform NVIDIA's flagship GPU on raw silicon, and Google has never competed chip-for-chip"* — it uses proprietary **OCS plus bidirectional (bidi) modules** (transmit and receive over one fibre, holding fibre count and cost per link down) to build a far larger scale-up domain and **compete at the cluster level on TCO**. ➤ **That is the cleanest one-line statement of why Google keeps buying optical dimensionality: a per-chip performance gap is offset by interconnect scale, and the price of that scale is a sustained rise in optical content.** Cross-read: [themes/custom-asic-tpu](themes/custom-asic-tpu.md), [themes/optical-cpo](themes/optical-cpo.md), [[LITE]], [[COHR]], [[MRVL]], [[AXTI]].

The Epoch block above says of Google's datacentre backstop: *"a contingent, unquantified obligation — Epoch says 'part of' the losses and gives no cap, no fee and no accounting treatment, so it cannot be sized from this source."* **The FT sizes it, and from Google's own balance sheet: *"People familiar with the matter said the Big Tech company had so far backstopped **10 DEVELOPMENTS WITH 2.4GW OF POWER** for TPUs. Google's guarantees put it on the hook for **AS MUCH AS $44BN IF ALL THE LEASES GO BAD**, though it marks the liability at **$815MN ON ITS BALANCE SHEET**. It could also step into the leases itself."*** ➜ **So the shape is: notional worst case ~$44bn, carrying value $815mn — a ~54x gap between the tail and the mark. That is the number to track at each 10-Q, and it is the direct counterpart to [[AVGO]]'s $29bn reported maximum exposure on the compute leg.**
- ⚠️ **AND IT IS ALSO A SCOPE EXPANSION OVER EPOCH, NOT JUST A SIZING. Epoch's datacentre leg was FIVE projects / 1,428 MW critical IT / $15.183bn of project debt. The FT reports the same five as the identified subset — *"The FT identified **five projects with 1.4GW of power, which have raised $15bn of debt** with the support of Google's backstop"* — but says Google has backstopped **10 developments / 2.4GW** in total. **The five-project table on this page is therefore roughly HALF the programme by power. Do not treat $15.183bn as the total project debt behind Google's guarantee.**
- **THE COMPUTE LEG, RESTATED FROM THE PRIMARY — and note it is a PURCHASE PRICE, not a debt figure: *"In June, the first tranche of TPU hardware passed from Google through Broadcom into this financing blender. A special-purpose vehicle known as **COMPUTE SPV paid $35BN for roughly 1GW** of the AI hardware, representing **around 1MN TPUs**."*** ✅ **RECONCILES with what this page already carries and does NOT replace it: Epoch's $34.5bn is the DEBT committed against that hardware (A1 $6bn + A2 $24bn + B $4.5bn); the FT's $35bn is what the SPV PAID for it. Two different quantities describing one transaction — the same reconciliation this page already made between JPM's "$35B XPV/SPV" and Epoch's $34.5bn of debt.** 🆕 **NET-NEW: the ~1mn TPU unit count for ~1GW, the "Compute SPV" name, and the JUNE date of the first tranche.**
- 🆕 **NET-NEW STRUCTURE THE EPOCH BLOCK DOES NOT HAVE: (a) **MORGAN STANLEY arranged the private-credit vehicle** — *"Morgan Stanley helped arrange a private-credit vehicle, funded by outside investors, that buys the chips and leases them to Anthropic in an adaptation of the **VENDOR-FINANCING MODEL BOEING AND GE BUILT** to sell aircraft and engines"* (Epoch named Apollo/Blackstone/global banks as the money, not MS as the arranger); (b) the backstop has a NAME and a DECAY — *"The arrangement, known as **RESIDUAL VALUE SUPPORT**, covers about **$30bn of the $35bn financing**, with Broadcom's exposure **declining as Anthropic makes its lease payments**"*; (c) the RISK ALLOCATION in one line — ***"Google guarantees the data centres. Broadcom commits to buying the chips and helps finance them. Apollo and Blackstone provide much of the private-credit capital that purchases the hardware before leasing it to Anthropic"***, with a Google executive quoted: *"This is each of us putting our balance sheet to work. We're doing it on the data centre side, [Broadcom's] doing it on the chip side."*
- 🔴🔴 **★ THE FORWARD LEG, WHICH IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE ADD AND IS NOT IN THE EPOCH NOTE AT ALL: *"The largest deal yet came together in **APRIL** when Google agreed to sell **ANOTHER 3.5GW of TPU hardware to Broadcom** for deployment by Anthropic. Broadcom's filings disclose **$128BN of purchase commitments, with $55.2BN of deliveries scheduled for its 2027 fiscal year and $72.9BN for 2028**. People familiar with the arrangements said those commitments relate **ALMOST ENTIRELY to its agreed purchase of 3.5GW of TPU hardware from Google**."*** ➜ **This page has carried the 3.5GW '27 / ~4GW '28 TPU majority from MS (07-23) and the $195-205B capex guide as separate objects. The FT ties the [[AVGO]] purchase-commitment disclosure — the same $128.1bn / $55.2bn FY27 / $72.9bn FY28 the [[AVGO]] page carries from Wells Fargo (08-18) — to Google TPU hardware specifically. It is the cleanest available cross-check that the TPU backlog on this page is a CONTRACTED supply obligation and not a forecast.** **Running total: *"the 4.5GW of TPU hardware they've agreed to sell"* (1GW done + 3.5GW agreed), against which *"The Google team is now racing to put together additional data centre projects with enough power"* — the Google executive: *"We're spending a lot of time on [power] right now — all of our time."*
- 🆕 **THE COST-OF-CAPITAL EDGE, QUANTIFIED — a genuinely new competitive datapoint for this page: *"Data centre projects backed by Google borrowed at a **MEDIAN RATE OF 7.1 PER CENT, compared with 9.3 PER CENT for the NEOCLOUD OPERATORS building around Nvidia's chips.** Jefferies analysts called this gap **'a structural cost-of-capital disadvantage'** for those in Nvidia's orbit."*** ➜ **A ~220bp funding advantage, sourced to actual borrowing rather than to a ratings argument — and it is the mechanism behind the Ben Thompson "fund the capital fight at a lower cost of capital" claim already on this page (08-18).**
- 🆕 **THE POWER SOURCING, AND THE EQUITY KICKER: the Google executive — *"We have a schedule and we're looking for capacity that will fit the schedule. **CRYPTO MINERS with excess capacity were helpful.**"* **TeraWulf was the first mover: *"a small outfit called TeraWulf the first to land a Google backstop to add a **360MW** data centre on its campus in upstate New York… Google guaranteed the lease payments on the Anthropic-bound site, which **Morgan Stanley packaged into a construction bond that in October raised $3.2BN** to get it built. In return for the backstop, **GOOGLE TOOK PENNY WARRANTS that gave it a stake in TeraWulf**."* Then *"Cipher Digital and Hut 8"* in Texas and Louisiana.** 🆕 **The penny-warrant equity participation is net-new here: Google is not only lending credit, it is taking equity upside for doing so — which changes the characterisation of the backstop from pure contingent liability to a priced trade.**
- ⚠️🔴 **A GENUINE NUMERICAL CONFLICT TO CARRY UNRESOLVED, NOT NET: the SAME TeraWulf/Lake Mariner site now has THREE different power figures on this page — **FT 360MW** (08-04), **Barclays Figure 7 366MW** (08-20, see the credit block below) and **Epoch 378 MW of CRITICAL IT** (08-12). The $3.2bn debt figure is identical in all three. The likeliest explanation is different bases (contracted power vs critical IT load vs nameplate), but no source states its basis, so all three are held and none is adopted.**
- ⚠️ **UNIT DISCIPLINE, RESTATED FOR THE NEW NUMBERS — four distinct quantities now circulate on this programme and conflating any two of them is the error to avoid: ① **>$150bn of AI CHIPS SUPPLIED** to Anthropic (FT headline claim — chip/hardware value); ② **~$200bn of CONTRACTS** in the programme, *"with roughly FOUR-FIFTHS tied to the chips themselves"* (FT — total contract notional, so ~$160bn of it is the chip leg); ③ **~$50bn of DEBT RAISED** behind the buildout (Epoch, 08-12 — $34.5bn compute + $15.183bn datacentre); ④ **$35bn PAID by Compute SPV** for the first ~1GW / ~1mn TPUs (FT — a purchase price). **A chip value is not a contract notional is not a debt quantum is not a purchase price. Never net ① against ③, and do not read the FT's larger numbers as superseding Epoch's smaller ones — they measure different things.** ⚠️ **Also do NOT chain $35bn ÷ 1GW into any capex-per-GW or content-per-GW mark on this page or on [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md): it is a grossed-up rack-system SALE PRICE from Google to an SPV, not a build cost.**
- **THE CONCENTRATION RISK, IN THE FT'S OWN FRAMING: *"For Google's project, the risk is big if concentrated: $200bn of contracts tied to Anthropic's ability to pay its chip and data centre leases."* And Jefferies' Jonathan Petersen on the industry-level version: *"There's a whole world that's been built underneath those companies, and if their appetite to invest decreases, all of it sees a slowdown. That's the big macro risk."*** **Background the FT supplies: TPUs are *"AI chips it has co-developed with Broadcom since 2016,"* once largely internal, now sold externally in *"pods"* — *"server racks taller than a person that connect thousands of chips into a single computing system."***

**🆕 2026-08-10 — the AI leadership exodus, and the contrarian read (FundaAI Research, 2026-08-10).** The facts as reported: **Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, Oriol Vinyals and several others are leaving**; **Demis Hassabis moves from CEO of Google DeepMind to Chair and Alphabet Chief Scientist**, with **Koray Kavukcuoglu taking on more of the day-to-day operating responsibility.** The market read it as a major brain drain.

FundaAI's dissent — *"The Market Sees Brain Drain; We See a Long-Overdue Organizational Consolidation"* — rests on three claims worth testing rather than accepting:
1. **Many of the departing seniors had already become peripheral to the core Gemini / frontier-LLM effort** over the past year or two — the distinction being between "the people who were historically most important to Google AI" and "the people actually driving frontier-model execution today."
2. **The real problem started *after* Gemini 3's success**, not with these departures: with arguably the leading multimodal model, best-in-class proprietary compute, and Nobel-level recognition for AlphaFold, the organisation concluded the frontier race was caught up, and **redirected its most exceptional talent toward AI-for-Science / drug discovery** — away from the engineering-heavy work of frontier-model scaling.
3. **That was the strategic misread**, on their argument: the path runs **scale compute → scale coding → scale agent harnesses → scale automated AI R&D → recursive self-improvement (RSI)**, and **AI-for-Science should sit on top of the RSI engine, not compete with it** — *"the ultimate form of AI for Science may not be scientists using AI to do science; it may be building an AI scientist whose own research capabilities improve over time."* Their framing of what OpenAI and Anthropic demonstrated is precisely this industrial-scaling path.

**How to use it:** this is the bull case for the reorg — that the bottleneck was organisational rather than talent, and consolidation under Koray refocuses execution on the scaling path. It is also, read the other way, a statement that **Google mis-allocated its best researchers for roughly two years** while competitors compounded — which is a bear datapoint dressed as a bull one. The testable prediction is straightforward: **the next Gemini release cadence and coding/agentic benchmark position**. Cross-ref [ANTHROPIC.md](ANTHROPIC.md), [OPENAI.md](OPENAI.md).

- **Consolidated revenue $119.8B, +24% (+23% cc); operating income +30% to $40.8B and operating margin +2pp to 34.0%.** This was Alphabet's 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth. GAAP EPS was $9.11, but a net unrealized equity-security gain contributed $6.26/share after tax; EPS excluding only that disclosed gain was approximately $2.85 (derived from company figures, not a fully normalized EPS). (Alphabet 2Q26 earnings release, 2026-07-22)
- **Search & Other +17% to $63.3B; YouTube ads +13% to $11.1B; Services +15% to $94.5B with 41.8% segment margin.** Search was in line with the +17% buyside bogey and about +0.4pp above JPM's +16.6% estimate using Alphabet's rounded headline growth; YouTube beat JPM's +8.6% / buyside +10% bars by about +4.4pp / +3.0pp on the same rounded basis. Management said popular AI features are driving query growth; World Cup-related YouTube videos reached 1.7B+ unique viewers. (Alphabet 2Q26 release/slides, 2026-07-22; JPM · Anmuth, 2026-07-14; BofA · Fenske, 2026-07-12)

The release attributes the acceleration to enterprise AI solutions, enterprise AI infrastructure and core GCP; it does not disclose the TPU-system revenue contribution. - **🆕 TPU-as-a-Service — the P&L revisions and the PT mechanic (Barclays · Ross Sandler, "Unpacking TPU-As-A-Service", 2026-07-24).** _The full structure, unit economics and GW ramp for this note are already laid out in the "TPU-as-a-Service / merchant TPU sales sized" bullet under Capstone estimates below — this bullet carries only what that one doesn't: the consolidated estimate changes, the PT mechanic, and a figure discrepancy to resolve._ Consolidated revisions on a full model rebuild: **total Alphabet revenue +12% to $650B in '27 (from $580B)** and **+40% to $950B in '28 (from $680B)**; **EBITDA +7% ('27) / +23% ('28)**; **EPS FY27 $15.40 (from $13.94)** and **FY28 $21.88 (from $15.98)**; effect on consensus — could **lift '28 consensus gross profit ~15% and operating income by more**. **The PT mechanic matters: $425 (OW) is held in level but is now struck on a 2027 multiple rather than a blended 27/28** — so the unchanged PT is not an unchanged view, it is the valuation year moving forward. Per Barclays' own desk, Sandler "**is the only analyst on Wall Street that is modeling out the revenues from TPUs**" (Barclays desk · Justin Kantrowitz, 2026-07-24). ⚠️ **Figure to reconcile before using:** Sandler's evidence line cites "**the $811B (up +$479B Q/Q) in purchase commitments buried in the 10-Q this week**," which does **not** tie to the Capstone 10-Q diff above — that reads **$232.7B → $707.0B (+$474B)** off the filing itself. The sequential deltas nearly agree (+$479B vs +$474B) but the absolute base differs by ~$104B, likely a broader aggregation (operating-lease and/or energy commitments). **Use the $707.0B filing figure as the house number**; treat $811B as Barclays' basis. Worth resolving at the next filing.
- **🆕 The other side of the same print — GOOG -6.9% on 07-23, and the buy-side is treating it as a source of funds (Barclays desk · Justin Kantrowitz, 2026-07-24).** The tape: **GOOG -6.9%** on 07-23 (alongside TSLA -14.5%, SPX -1.2%, NDX -1.9%; Rothschild & Co · Adley, 2026-07-24), and per the FT, "Google burning through cash for the first time since going public decades ago as it raised its spending forecast for AI infrastructure" (@FT, 2026-07-23). At times like this, investors seem to only focus on the balance sheet impact and seem to [be] missing the potential ramp in revenues that are coming."** Also flagged: with oil back above $100, names with fuel exposure (**AMZN, DASH, [[UBER]]**) should underperform. - **Axion custom Arm CPU — silicon franchise widening (SemiAnalysis "CPUs are Back", 2026-02-09):** Google's custom-CPU line for GCP, announced 2024 / GA 2025. **C4A**: up to 72 Neoverse V2 cores, standard mesh, 8ch DDR5 + PCIe5, large monolithic 5nm die — SemiAnalysis *estimates* (analyst inference from Cloud Next 2024 wafer images, **not a confirmed Google spec**) the die prints 81 cores in a 9×9 mesh with 9 disabled for yield. SemiAnalysis further *believes* (analyst inference, **not confirmed Google roadmap**) a new 3nm die was designed for a 96-core C4A bare-metal instance in preview late 2025. **N4A** (cost-effective scale-out/microservices tier): now in preview, 64 lower-perf Neoverse N3 cores on a much smaller full-custom TSMC 3nm die, "allowing significant volume ramps through 2026" (SemiAnalysis, 2026-02-09). **Vertical-integration trajectory — Axion has moved to Full COT (SemiAnalysis "EDA Market Primer", 2026-05-21, light read-through folded 2026-07-24):** ~99% of hyperscaler ASIC silicon today runs **Hybrid COT** (customer owns architecture + IP selection, a vendor handles physical implementation) at an estimated **1.2x EDA premium** over a pure vendor-designed ASIC; **Full COT** — where the customer licenses the Synopsys or Cadence stack directly — carries an estimated **1.6x premium**, and SemiAnalysis names **"Google moving Axion in-house last quarter"** alongside Apple M-series and Tesla AI4-AI6 as the Full-COT cohort. One line, but it dates a real step up Google's vertical-integration curve on the CPU side (more EDA/tooling cost carried in-house, less dependence on a design-service middleman) and is the CPU-side analogue of the TPU-COT/MediaTek dual-sourcing already on this page. (SemiAnalysis, 2026-05-21) [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_05_21_ENC_EDA_Market_Primer_email.html) TPU volumes are the #2 driver of HBM bit demand after Nvidia (via the Broadcom ASIC partnership) — detail on AVGO's page. TPU design philosophy prioritizes *reliability* — deliberately non-aggressive vs merchant GPUs on redline features like compute-in-base-die (SemiAnalysis "Scaling the Memory Wall: The Rise and Roadmap of HBM", 2026-02-09). **Read-through (Bernstein · David Dai/Rasgon "The CPU Renaissance? $223bn TAM", 2026-06-17):** independently sizes the Axion program — **Axion C4A = 72 Neoverse V3 cores (TSMC 5nm)**, **~21% of GCP instances**, and **TPU7x runs 1 CPU : 4 TPU** — corroborating the Arm-CPU/head-node ratio on the page (Bernstein's V3 core-arch label differs from SemiAnalysis's V2 characterization above; both retained). [Bernstein CPU](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Bernstein_on_CPU.html)

The expert estimates **~$85B of TPU dollars entered the 1Q26 backlog** (vs ~$11.5B in 4Q25), reflecting ~4GW of Anthropic TPU orders; stripping TPUs out leaves **~$365B of "pure" cloud backlog (+$134B q/q)**, implying ex-TPU cloud growth of ~70%/62% in CY26/27 and a TPU-driven capex-est raise toward **~$290B+ for FY27**. Also: **first quarter with no buyback since COVID** (100% capital-allocation focus on capacity), and the 1Q 10-Q disclosed Google providing **credit backstops to third-party data centers/power infrastructure** tied to these deals. Product: **Gemini 3.5 Flash** called "a benchmaxxed prop" performing far worse than GPT-5.6 / Opus 4.8 in real-world use; **3.5 Pro "not even Opus level on coding."** Google also **recently lost more RL talent to Anthropic** and its **RL efforts are "too decentralized."** Punchline: **"the race for 3rd is currently between Meta and SpaceX, not Google"** — advice: start having SWEs build RL tasks and redistribute much more compute to DeepMind immediately. **Verbatim framing added on the 2026-07-24 dedup pass (previously paraphrased only):** SemiAnalysis's opening frame is that frontier AI "has increasingly felt like **a two horse race between OpenAI vs Anthropic**. Google had a brief moment in the spotlight with **Gemini 3 Pro and Nano Banana, but they've since faded dramatically.** Despite their **Windsurf acquisition, they're far from a compelling agentic coding product**, and **3.5 Flash is a benchmaxxed prop that performs far worse than GPT 5.6 and Opus 4.8 in real world scenarios** (much less Fable and 5.6). **3.5 Pro is not even Opus level on coding**" — with Microsoft judged to have "completely blown their early lead with GitHub Copilot," Chinese labs "too compute poor," and Meta framed as the most plausible third entrant. **Log it as the harsh, independent, attributed view it is — this page does NOT adopt it.** It sits directly against what the page argues elsewhere: Gemini is the clear #2 and gaining on gen-AI web-traffic share (9.1%→27.8% over 12 months, @Similarweb 07-15), Gemini app hit 950M MAU with DAU tripling y/y and AI Mode 1B+ MAU (Q2'26 call), Google is the only lab shipping full any-to-any multimodal (@emollick 07-13), and the Q2 print delivered Cloud +82% with a $514B backlog. The part of the SemiAnalysis critique the Q2 call itself *conceded* is the narrow one: **the coding gap is acknowledged by management**, 3.5 Pro is still only "in testing," and Gemini 4 pretraining has only just begun — so treat the piece as a well-informed hostile read on **coding/agentic model quality and RL organisation**, not as a verdict on the franchise. Also from the same note, a supply-side datapoint relevant to Google's compute sourcing: **SpaceXAI is selling ~$26B a year of GPUs to Anthropic/Google** — the counterparty scale behind the ~$920M/month SpaceX rental already on this page. SpaceX's **Google** deal is priced at **4x peers' revenue per MW** (the Anthropic deal at 3x) — and "**SpaceX's pricing on the Google deal is even higher than what we observe on the on-demand or short-term rental market**"; because the cost structure is roughly the same, the profit-per-MW gap is wider still. - **🔴 THE SPACEX COMPUTE PRICE FINALLY HAS A DOLLAR NUMBER — AND IT DOES NOT AGREE WITH THE RATIO THIS PAGE HAS BEEN CARRYING (Arete Research · Andrew Beale / Alex Pound / Pierre-Marie d'Ornano / Frederik Strauss, "NEO Clouds: Greater Pricing Power", 2026-08-21).** Arete estimates **[[SPCX]] is selling GB300s to Google at ~$55m/MW**, against **~$31m/MW for the largely last-gen Hopper inference capacity it sells [[ANTHROPIC]]**, with **[[CRWV]] and [[NBIS]] now achieving $20-25m/MW** and SpaceX pricing short-term compute at **2-4x historic 5-yr NEO take-or-pay rates**. ⚠️⚠️ **UNIT HAZARD, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE LINE: $55m/MW IS REVENUE PER MW FROM SPACEX'S SIDE — i.e. THE CONTRACT PRICE GOOGLE PAYS FOR COMPUTE. It is NOT capex per MW, NOT a build cost and NOT a Google capital-intensity figure. It must NEVER be netted against the $30–35bn/GW Alphabet capex-per-GW anchor, the ~$11m/MW Fluidstack project-DEBT-per-MW figure below, or any $/GW build-cost mark on [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md), and it must never be chained into a capex series.** ⚠️ **OPEN DIVERGENCE, DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED: Arete's $55m/MW against a $20-25m/MW peer base implies roughly **2.2-2.8x** peer revenue/MW, whereas SemiAnalysis (07-02, bullet above) put the same Google deal at **4x** peers and the Anthropic deal at 3x — Arete's own $31m/MW Anthropic mark is ~1.2-1.6x on its peer base. Both houses run proprietary deal databases, seven weeks apart, on peer sets they define differently; NEITHER MARK IS AVERAGED AND NEITHER SUPERSEDES THE OTHER. What they agree on is the sign and the mechanism: Google is paying a large premium for short-tenor, latest-generation capacity, and it chose to do that rather than sell that capacity itself.** **Context from the same note, which is why the premium is holding: compute supply is "unlikely to catch up soon" — gated by WAFER and POWER constraints with US states SLOWING data-center permitting — and "any AI cloud player not completely sold out can sell compute at very attractive prices."** (Arete Research "NEO Clouds: Greater Pricing Power", 2026-08-21) [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/20260821_Arete_Research_NEO_Clouds-_Greater_Pricing_Power.html)
